value.rationale: PASS: The first positive-characteristic prime merges two representatives whose complex complements constitute a nontrivial Zariski pair, a structurally important boundary for specialization of arrangement geometry. The complete support/contact degeneration table distinguishes separate collision mechanisms at 7,11,109, and rules out all other bad primes for this fixed integral model. A named exact singularity classification of a natural published geometric family can be useful even though its field-splitting corollary is a routine consequence of prior eliminants.

final_claim: For four explicitly fixed integral three-conic-one-line degree-seven divisors, exactly the primes 7,11 and additionally 109 for arrangement H1 change the geometric singular-support incidence among primes p>=7; at p=7 H1=H4 as reduced divisors, at p=11 characteristic triple contacts jump, and at p=109 H1 acquires a line-conic tangency. For good primes their rational singular supports have counts (9+(109/p), 9+(-11/p), 10,10), with all four Frobenius sign pairs of natural density 1/4.
limitations: Only the displayed integral equations and p>=7; p=2,3,5 are outside domain.
Geometric reduced support and smooth-branch contact, not full singular subschemes, Milnor/Tjurina invariants, or finite-field topology.
Infinite-prime statements use explicit factors and Chebotarev, not sampled Fp counts.
